results.name: in_range_nonrule_same_digit_sets
results.description: For 3-4 example sets whose examples all share one last digit, yes-rate for targets strictly inside the [min,max] range that do NOT share that last digit; observed > null means people still accept in-range numbers (interval-like generalization) when a sharp digit rule fits, more than the model's rule-dominated posterior allows (observed < null: humans stricter).
results.code:
# name: in_range_nonrule_same_digit_sets
# description: For 3-4 example sets whose examples all share one last digit, yes-rate for targets strictly inside the [min,max] range that do NOT share that last digit; observed > null means people still accept in-range numbers (interval-like generalization) when a sharp digit rule fits, more than the model's rule-dominated posterior allows (observed < null: humans stricter).
def test_statistic(df):
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(df["number_set"].astype(str))
    E = pd.Series(uniq).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)[codes]
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    ld = np.mod(E, 10)
    same = (n >= 3) & (np.nanmin(ld, axis=1) == np.nanmax(ld, axis=1))
    lo = np.nanmin(E, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    m = same & (t > lo) & (t < hi) & (np.mod(t, 10) != np.nanmin(ld, axis=1))
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: shared_last_digit_far_target
results.description: For 2-4 example sets whose examples all share one last digit, yes-rate for targets with that same last digit lying more than 10 outside the set's range; observed < null means people extend a last-digit rule to far targets less than the model's rule posterior predicts (observed > null: more).
results.code:
# name: shared_last_digit_far_target
# description: For 2-4 example sets whose examples all share one last digit, yes-rate for targets with that same last digit lying more than 10 outside the set's range; observed < null means people extend a last-digit rule to far targets less than the model's rule posterior predicts (observed > null: more).
def test_statistic(df):
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(df["number_set"].astype(str))
    E = pd.Series(uniq).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)[codes]
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    ld = np.mod(E, 10)
    same = (n >= 2) & (np.nanmin(ld, axis=1) == np.nanmax(ld, axis=1))
    lo = np.nanmin(E, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    far = (t < lo - 10) | (t > hi + 10)
    m = same & far & (np.mod(t, 10) == np.nanmin(ld, axis=1))
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: shared_tens_digit_outside
results.description: Among targets outside the set's [min,max] range and not examples, yes-rate for targets sharing a tens digit (same decade, 100 counted as 10) with some example minus targets sharing none, restricted to targets within 10 of the nearest example; observed > null means people generalize by decade membership more than the model's decade-aligned interval bonus captures.
results.code:
# name: shared_tens_digit_outside
# description: Among targets outside the set's [min,max] range and not examples, yes-rate for targets sharing a tens digit (same decade, 100 counted as 10) with some example minus targets sharing none, restricted to targets within 10 of the nearest example; observed > null means people generalize by decade membership more than the model's decade-aligned interval bonus captures.
def test_statistic(df):
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(df["number_set"].astype(str))
    E = pd.Series(uniq).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)[codes]
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(E, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    out = (t < lo) | (t > hi)
    d = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    near = out & (d <= 10) & (d > 0)
    shared = np.any(np.floor(E / 10) == np.floor(t / 10)[:, None], axis=1)
    a = near & shared; b = near & ~shared
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: unanimous_no_cell_fraction
results.description: Fraction of distinct (set, target) cells in which every response is "no"; observed > null means people reject clearly-out-of-concept targets more uniformly than the model's guessing/stray-example noise allows (observed < null: humans noisier than the model).

results.name: even_target_bias_mixed_sets
results.description: For sets of 2+ examples containing both odd and even numbers, yes-rate for even non-example targets minus odd ones; observed > null means people favour even targets beyond any rule the examples support (observed < null: favour odd), a stimulus bias the model lacks.
results.code:
# name: even_target_bias_mixed_sets
# description: For sets of 2+ examples containing both odd and even numbers, yes-rate for even non-example targets minus odd ones; observed > null means people favour even targets beyond any rule the examples support (observed < null: favour odd), a stimulus bias the model lacks.
def test_statistic(df):
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(df["number_set"].astype(str))
    E = pd.Series(uniq).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)[codes]
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    p = np.mod(E, 2)
    mixed = (n >= 2) & (np.nanmin(p, axis=1) != np.nanmax(p, axis=1))
    notin = ~np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    ev = np.mod(t, 2) == 0
    a = mixed & notin & ev; b = mixed & notin & ~ev
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: above_minus_below_range
results.description: Among targets outside the set's [min,max] range by 1-30, yes-rate for targets above the max minus targets below the min; observed > null means people extend concepts upward (toward larger numbers) more than downward beyond what the model's interval prior predicts (observed < null: the reverse).
results.code:
# name: above_minus_below_range
# description: Among targets outside the set's [min,max] range by 1-30, yes-rate for targets above the max minus targets below the min; observed > null means people extend concepts upward (toward larger numbers) more than downward beyond what the model's interval prior predicts (observed < null: the reverse).
def test_statistic(df):
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(df["number_set"].astype(str))
    E = pd.Series(uniq).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)[codes]
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(E, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    a = (t > hi) & (t - hi <= 30)
    b = (t < lo) & (lo - t <= 30)
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: gap_middle_vs_edge
results.description: For 2-example sets whose examples are at least 20 apart, among non-example targets strictly between them, yes-rate for targets within 5 of an example minus targets more than 5 from both; observed > null means people's gap-filling decays with distance from the examples (similarity) more than the model's flat interval membership predicts (observed < null: the middle is favoured).
results.code:
# name: gap_middle_vs_edge
# description: For 2-example sets whose examples are at least 20 apart, among non-example targets strictly between them, yes-rate for targets within 5 of an example minus targets more than 5 from both; observed > null means people's gap-filling decays with distance from the examples (similarity) more than the model's flat interval membership predicts (observed < null: the middle is favoured).
def test_statistic(df):
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(df["number_set"].astype(str))
    E = pd.Series(uniq).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)[codes]
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    lo = np.nanmin(E, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    m = (n == 2) & (hi - lo >= 20) & (t > lo) & (t < hi)
    d = np.minimum(t - lo, hi - t)
    a = m & (d <= 5); b = m & (d > 5)
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: inset_target_yes_rate
results.description: Yes-rate on trials whose target is itself one of the shown examples; observed < null means people deny shown examples more often than the model (which treats examples as near-certain members) predicts, observed > null means the model under-endorses them.
results.code:
# name: inset_target_yes_rate
# description: Yes-rate on trials whose target is itself one of the shown examples; observed < null means people deny shown examples more often than the model (which treats examples as near-certain members) predicts, observed > null means the model under-endorses them.
def test_statistic(df):
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(df["number_set"].astype(str))
    E = pd.Series(uniq).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)[codes]
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    m = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0
